title: MolarMasses
description: The app's molar-mass reference data, schema 1: web/public/data/molar-masses.json. This is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for every mass↔molar conversion factor the app uses — the mass/molar LOINC sibling table and the computed indices both derive their factors from it, and no factor is written by hand anywhere in TypeScript. A factor is never stored: what is stored is a molar mass, and `web/src/data/molarMasses.ts` turns it into a factor for a given unit pair, so "38.67 mg/dL per mmol/L" cannot drift from "cholesterol is 386.664 g/mol". Each molar mass is in turn derived from a molecular formula and the atomic weights in `atomicWeights`, both of which carry the source they were verified against, so the whole chain from an IUPAC atomic weight to a number in a chart is auditable. Like the analyte catalog this is app-internal data with no outside authors, so the objects are CLOSED: a mistyped key fails the conformance suite instead of being silently ignored at runtime.

atomicWeights.title: AtomicWeights
atomicWeights.description: The standard atomic weights every molar mass below is computed from. Present so that a molar mass is never an unexplained constant: it is a formula plus this table.

source.description: Where the whole table was taken from. One source for all elements, because they come from one published table.

fullTableUrl.description: Optional. The unabridged table, for the elements whose value is taken from it rather than from the abridged one.

elements.description: Keyed by element symbol. Only the elements the tabulated analytes are made of — this is not a periodic table.

date.description: ISO date the source was actually retrieved. A citation nobody fetched is not a citation.

atomicWeight.title: AtomicWeight
atomicWeight.description: One element's standard atomic weight, as used in this project's molar-mass arithmetic.

value.description: The single number used in the arithmetic. For an element CIAAW publishes as an interval this is the abridged conventional value, not an endpoint of the interval.

publishedAs.description: Verbatim as CIAAW prints it — an interval in brackets, or a value with its parenthesised uncertainty. Kept as text so the published form is visible next to the single number this project collapses it to.

table.description: Which CIAAW table `value` came from: the abridged (conventional) table for an element published as an interval, the full table for an element published as a single value with an uncertainty.

note.description: Optional. Why this element needed a judgement call.

molarMass.title: MolarMass
molarMass.description: One analyte's molar mass, and the evidence for it. An entry exists because some conversion in the app needs it — a mass/molar LOINC sibling pair, or a computed index whose formula wants an input in the other unit system.

id.description: Stable key the TypeScript side names this entry by. Not a LOINC: several LOINC codes share one molar mass (total, HDL and LDL cholesterol are all cholesterol).

name.description: How a Reference Book page prints it.

formula.description: Molecular formula in Hill order, or a bare element symbol. `molarMassGPerMol` must be reproducible from this formula and the `atomicWeights` table — the conformance suite recomputes it, so the two cannot drift.

molarMassGPerMol.description: Grams per mole, computed from `formula` and `atomicWeights`, rounded to 6 decimals. The only number in this file that a conversion factor is built from; every factor in the app is this value scaled by the two units' decimal prefixes.

basis.description: How honest the number is. `compound` — a single molecular species, so the molar mass is exact. `element` — the analyte is an element measured as itself, so the value is its atomic weight. `conventional` — there is no single true molar mass and clinical practice agrees on a stand-in (a mixture reported on one representative species, or a value reported on an atom count rather than a molecule). A `conventional` entry MUST carry a `note` saying what the convention is.

note.description: Optional for `compound` and `element`, required for `conventional`. States what is approximate and why, in the entry itself rather than in a comment somewhere downstream.

sources.description: Every source actually retrieved for this entry. A compound cites PubChem for its identity and formula; an element cites CIAAW for its atomic weight.

source.title: Source
source.description: One retrieved citation. Every field is something a reader can check without trusting this file.

identifier.description: The stable identifier within that authority — a PubChem CID, or the named CIAAW entry.

reportedMolarMassGPerMol.description: Optional. The mass the source itself prints for THIS entry's species, at the source's own precision — PubChem rounds to four significant figures and computes on an older set of atomic weights, so this will not equal `molarMassGPerMol` exactly. The conformance suite requires the two to agree within 0.05%, which is loose enough for that rounding and tight enough to catch a wrong formula or a transposed digit. Absent where the source is identity evidence rather than a mass to compare against — urea nitrogen cites urea's PubChem entry to establish that each molecule carries two nitrogen atoms, and no source anywhere reports "28.014 g/mol of urea nitrogen". Every `compound` and `element` entry must carry it on at least one source.
